## ChatOSS v1.18.1

A Launch-mode fix release. Agents that had finished now actually say so, the setup pause asks about one agent at a time, and terminal agents are back on **auto** rather than a permission bypass nobody chose.

### Terminal agents stayed "working" after they finished

Agents whose own screens read *"Done. Nothing is pending."* sat blue and **WORKING** for as long as you left them — the Launch agent was told the same thing, and the stall nudge typed *"are you still working?"* at agents that had answered minutes earlier. Two independent bugs, both fixed:

- The "is it parked at its prompt?" check tested only the **last non-empty line** of the screen. Claude Code draws a border and a footer *under* its input box, so the line it tested was `⏵⏵ bypass permissions on…` instead of the `❯` two rows above — false for every Claude Code agent ever launched.
- The internal "a dialog is up" flag was a one-way latch: set when an agent booted into a dialog, never cleared. That disabled *both* of the other ways an agent can be recognised as finished, so with the first bug live, "finished" was unreachable.

### "Auto-merged into main when it finished." repeating forever

An agent's status could oscillate between working and idle, and each entry re-ran the merge — one `git merge` of an already-merged branch per cycle, with the green message reappearing each time. A merge now stands down until the agent is actually sent more work.

### Permissions: auto, not bypass

Terminal agents shipped with the CLI's full permission bypass. They now run in **auto mode** — they approve their own file edits, so they never stall on "do you want to make this edit?", and they **ask before running commands**. When one asks, it comes to you in the chat to approve or decline, and the Launch agent answers the terminal for you.

**Settings → Launch → "Auto-approve everything terminal agents ask"** turns the bypass back on if you want it. OpenCode was a silent bypass too (its generated config pre-allowed shell commands) and now follows the same switch.

### Setup: one agent per card

The "which CLI?" pause is now one card **per agent**, shown in turn, each with that agent's **full task** and its own CLI, model and reasoning effort — pre-filled with what it would have run anyway. **"Use this CLI + model + effort for the rest of this conversation's terminal agents"** answers every remaining agent, so a batch of eight is still one decision if you want it to be. The previous single card squeezed every agent into a scroll box and cut each task to one line, which meant choosing a model without seeing what it was for.

### Also

- **The Launch agent has full control of its terminals**, and now knows it. Asked to move a struggling agent onto a different model, it used to answer "a CLI's model is pinned at launch" and close the agent — throwing away everything it had learned. It isn't pinned: ChatOSS advertises every one of your models to each CLI, so `/model` works, and the agent can drive any of the CLI's own commands and menus.
- A terminal card that went black while you resized cards or switched views can no longer be blanked by the paint watchdog rebuilding it from an empty replay, and resizing no longer looks like a frozen terminal to that watchdog.
- `chatoss launch --auto-approve-all` for the same choice from your own terminal.

After updating, reinstall the `chatoss` command from **Settings → Launch** if you use Launch mode from a terminal (the bundled CLI is refreshed with the app; a stale copy elsewhere on PATH is not).
